name: O.D.I.N. v2.4.1
body:
Security fix: ODIN no longer writes notification tokens (Telegram, Discord, Slack and other webhooks) into its own log files, and removes the ones already written.

### Security

- ODIN wrote the address of every notification it sent into its own log files. For Telegram, Discord, Slack and other webhook notifications that address contains the secret token, so the token could be read in the log files in ODIN's data folder, in the administrator log viewer and in a troubleshooting report. This affects ODIN 2.1.0 to 2.4.0 on installs that send notifications to those services. ODIN no longer logs these addresses, hides them wherever logs are shown, and removes the lines already written from its log files the first time 2.4.1 starts. After updating, replace the bot token or webhook address of each such notification channel with a new one, especially if you have shared a log file or a troubleshooting report. Backups made by ODIN do not contain log files.

name: O.D.I.N. v2.4.0
body:
Reminders for paused prints, Plate cleared on printer cards, filament deductions that stay with the physical print, the Fjord theme, a per-job Timeline, AMS humidity as a percentage.

### Added

- AMS humidity now also shows as a percentage (Bambu AMS units that report it), in the web app, the API and the Home Assistant integration.
- ODIN can remind you when a print stays paused, with farm-wide timing settings and the recorded cause. Home Assistant shows pause duration, a Paused too long sensor, and a fleet count. Reminders follow Print Paused preferences and quiet hours.
- Printer cards and details now offer “Plate cleared” with a confirmation that says whether a waiting job will be released. A waiting job exists only where the installation's queue uses the `waiting_plate_clear` state; the standard PostgreSQL job enum does not include it. Home Assistant gains a Plate cleared button and a Plate needs clearing sensor, with the same state available on its Status entity.
- The print history API supports date range filters, paging, and a total count. Utilization now requests prints that ended within the selected period.
- Fjord theme with light and dark appearances, softer surfaces, and a preview in theme settings. High contrast keeps the Classic appearance. Theme family stays saved on this device.
- Timelapse cards show the print's name alongside its job number when you have access to the name. The timelapse list and detail API responses include `print_name`.
- Prints started at the printer now appear in job history on every printer type, not only Bambu.
- Skip objects (Experimental, Bambu Lab printers): while a print that ODIN started is running, choose objects on the plate to stop printing, from a numbered plate picture and a list on the printer page, on desktop and phone. It is off by default: a platform administrator turns it on per printer under Experimental features on the printer page. Built from how Bambu's own software sends this command and not yet verified on a real printer. API: `GET /api/printers/{id}/print-objects` lists the objects; `POST /api/printers/{id}/skip-objects` now requires `print_job_id` and is audited.
- Settle filament for an unresolved print by recording its spools and grams, reviewing manual use, or keeping an existing deduction. Archive records now explain why filament needs attention, with a filter and a dashboard link. Later weighing or measurement is checked before another deduction.
- Foundry Timeline now draws every scheduled job as its own bar, with a choice of 12 hours to 7 days, instead of one block per printer.

### Changed

- ODIN does slightly less work on every request and during alert delivery. Nothing behaves differently.
- Unknown status filters for spools, orders and job exports, and unknown alert type or severity filters, now return 422 with the allowed values on both PostgreSQL and SQLite. Previously PostgreSQL returned a server error and SQLite returned an empty list. Notification settings switches now announce the channel and alert name to screen readers, with setup requirements as descriptions.
- ODIN now stops at start-up on PostgreSQL 18 or newer with a clear message before changing the database, and asks you to use the PostgreSQL 16 server it ships with.
- Elegoo: when job sending is switched off, the refusal now explains that sending jobs is Experimental and that monitoring, pause, resume, speed and stop still work.

### Fixed

- Reports, analytics and the Home Assistant integration now show one number for prints that did not complete (failed plus stopped). Success rates use it, so they can be lower than before on farms that stop prints by hand. The failed and stopped counts are still there.
- Moonraker commands now preserve spaces, special characters and multiple lines when sent to a printer.
- Editing a spool's remaining weight now records balance decreases and an audit entry, rejects invalid balances, and warns before deducting filament already included in the edited balance.
- Weighing a spool without an empty-spool weight now explains how to enter it instead of failing; editing an unknown empty-spool weight no longer assumes 250 g.
- Clearing a printer's plate now records the current confirmation for prints started at the printer, even when they have no queued job. The printer card and Home Assistant show that confirmation until another print starts.
- PostgreSQL backups made by ODIN 2.0.16 to 2.0.44 now receive a clear refusal naming their release range and recovery steps, both when uploaded and when staged from the backup list. These older backups still require recovery on the release that made them before upgrading; the backup guide now explains how to cancel one left pending across an upgrade. SQLite is unaffected.
- Failed and cancelled Bambu prints now deduct the filament the AMS measured on installations without organizations; completed prints use the measured amount when there is one.
- A stuck start can now be released from Dispatch recovery after filament was moved or reloaded. Before, changing a slot's filament after a failed start blocked the release for good.
- Square stock replies now correctly report whether sending stock changes is enabled.
- AMS humidity labels now run from dry to wet correctly and show N/A when there is no sensor reading. API readers of `humidity_label` will see different, now correct, words.
- Elegoo: the switch that allows job sending (Experimental) was missing from the web app and could only be set through the API. It is now under Experimental features on the printer page.
- Recover past filament deductions recorded while an older version was running on an upgraded database, so those prints cannot be deducted again after upgrading.
- Keep filament deductions with the physical print, so deleting jobs, spools or archives cannot deduct the same print again. Check past usage before startup and preserve manual use for settlement review.

### Security

- Square setup delegation remains off by default. Tokens can now only add a mapping or first stock baseline; repeating the same mapping changes nothing. Baselines must match a live Square count and use a time within 15 minutes in the past or 60 seconds in the future. Permission is checked again before saving. Approval notes are stored exactly or refused if they resemble credentials, and setup audits record mappings and permission changes. Signed-in administrator workflows are unchanged.
- Square setup permission is off by default: no token receives it on upgrade. A signed-in administrator can grant or revoke `write:square_setup` for one personal API token to map products and record stock baselines in ODIN. Each delegated call records an approval note and the token's identity; the note is a record, not a verification. Neither operation writes to Square. Connection changes, activation, unmapping and addition review still require a signed-in administrator.
- Prints started at the printer now belong to the printer's organization, so other organizations cannot see their jobs.
- Only a signed-in platform administrator can change Education mode; each change records the previous and new values.

---

name: O.D.I.N. v2.3.0
body:
Print next from live stock, the real cost of every print, your farm's time zone, printer-reported failures, six more Bambu materials.

### Added

- If you stop a print because it was failing, you can now mark it as failed afterwards, with a reason. Failure counts and success rates then reflect what happened, and you can undo the change. Recorded filament and cost are not changed.
- Six more Bambu materials are recognised: ASA-CF, ASA Aero, PET-CF, PPA-CF, PPS-CF and TPU for AMS. On Bambu AMS printers and the Kobra S1, a print that needs one of them starts only when the slot reports exactly that material. Before, ODIN stored some under a similar material's name (for example PET-CF as PETG-CF) and then refused the print at the final check. Existing slots correct themselves on the next printer report or reassignment; imported catalogue entries previously marked Other are corrected automatically. Generic Moonraker printers still have no material-verification gate. Education continues to refuse abrasive materials, and Education AMS reads do not yet accept these six materials.
- Import your Bambu filament catalogue and pick spools by their exact Bambu name. ODIN shows that name on spools and slots; material checks before a print are unchanged.
- The status feed and the Home Assistant integration now report how many prints were stopped mid-run today, separate from failed prints.
- New: every finished print shows what it actually cost next to its estimate. On a finished job (the Cost link on its row in Jobs, and the job's detail in the Timeline) you see "Estimate $A, actual $B", the difference, and a breakdown: the filament each spool really gave, at the price that spool had when the print started; the hours the printer really ran, at your current electricity and machine rates; and labour, packaging, other costs and overhead from your pricing settings, marked as not measured. Failed and cancelled attempts are counted and listed, so the estimate's failure allowance is not added on top. When something was not recorded (for example a spool with no purchase price) the total is shown as "at least" with the reason, never as the full cost; a job finished by hand with no print on record says "no usage recorded". Nothing is shown until pricing has been saved. Free on every tier. `GET /api/v1/jobs/{id}/cost` returns the same figures to whoever may read the job; nothing new is stored. Pro: Analytics gains a "Cost per print" table by model or by product (pieces made, average actual cost per piece, the estimate, how far apart they are, and the share spent on failed attempts), with a CSV export, and each model card shows its average actual cost per piece. An average appears once a model or product has three completed prints with full cost records; prints with missing records are left out of it and counted beside it. School submissions are not included, and work limited to a group stays limited to that group. `GET /api/v1/analytics/cost-per-print?from=&to=&group=model|product` and `GET /api/v1/export/cost-per-print`.
- New: set your farm's time zone once (Settings > General). 'Completed today', daily totals and Home Assistant's day now follow it instead of UTC. Until an admin saves one, the day follows the time zone saved with the quiet hours if there is one, then the server's `TZ`, then UTC; the dashboard used to count from midnight UTC even when `TZ` was set, and now agrees with Home Assistant. The first admin to open Settings > General sees their browser's time zone offered and nothing is saved until they press the button. The dashboard names the farm zone on "Completed today" for a viewer in another zone, `GET /api/config` returns `farm_timezone` and `farm_timezone_effective`, and the Home Assistant status payload gains `timezone`. Saved quiet hours are not changed: a window saved without a time zone stays UTC, and Settings now offers the farm zone for it in one click.
- Home Assistant integration 0.3.0. Each printer now has a Spools loaded sensor that lists every spool slot (colour, name, material, how much is left), a Last print finished time and a Plate cleared time. The Next job sensor says how many more jobs are queued behind it, which spools are too low for it, and whether it is ready to start. A printer no longer shows as "error" in Home Assistant after its print went on to complete; the Status sensor also carries when the last print completed and when the last error was recorded. Other organizations' jobs and controlled work stay hidden as before, and spool amounts are not shown on a printer another organization shares with you. No extra polling: the integration still makes one status call.
- New (Pro): set a reorder point and target for each product. ODIN shows what to print next, ranked, from your live stock and open orders, and queues the plates in one click. Products gains a "Print next" list (`GET /api/production/replenishment`): stock is read from Square in one request per location at most every two minutes, and when Square cannot be read (or ITAR mode is on) the list shows the last recorded counts with their age. "Queue N plates" creates held jobs from the product's qualified recipe; nothing is queued automatically and Square is never written. The per-product policy now holds three numbers the owner sets (reorder point, target, smallest batch) instead of a fixed product category; policies saved earlier keep the numbers they already produced. The Home Assistant status gains `print_next_count` on Pro. Print next also respects restrictions attached to shared print files, including restrictions set by another organization: viewers without clearance cannot see work in progress, receive a print-next count in Home Assistant, or queue suggested plates. Production overview and history keep each recipe and receipt under its recorded ID, so prepared stock additions remain visible even when an older saved copy contains conflicting IDs.
- Quiet hours now follow your farm's clock. Settings > General saves a time zone with the quiet hours (taken from your browser when you save, and you can pick another), and the scheduler keeps to those clock times all year, including across daylight-saving changes. Quiet hours you saved before this update, and the server defaults, are still applied in UTC exactly as before: Settings says so and offers "Use my time zone (keeps the same clock hours)", which changes nothing until you press it and save. Quiet hours that are off stay off. `GET`/`PUT /api/config` carry the zone as `blackout_timezone`; an unknown zone name is refused.
- Dashboard: the fixed five-step tour is replaced by a "Getting started" card that shows what is actually done on your farm: a printer added, a printer online, a file uploaded, filament set on a slot, and a first job sent to a printer. Each line links to where it is done and ticks itself; the card goes away when everything is done or when you dismiss it (remembered per user). Viewers do not see it, and anyone who finished or skipped the old tour will not see it either.
- Models: until pricing has been saved, people who may edit pricing see "Set up pricing to see cost and price on each model" with a link to the Calculator. Saving pricing in the Calculator removes the line straight away.
- Models and Upload now say which of your printers a file runs on: "Runs on 3 of your printers" on the upload result and on each model card, with the printer names when you press it. When none fits, it says which printer the file was sliced for. The count uses the same checks as scheduling (printer type, file type, bed size, the printer model the file was sliced for, and a file uploaded for one printer), and only counts printers you can see. When exactly one printer fits, the Schedule Print dialog selects it for you; a printer you pick yourself, or Auto-assign, is kept. The same places also show what the file states about itself: nozzle size, layer height, plate type, supports on or off and filament colour. A detail the file does not state is left out instead of guessed (a new upload no longer records 0.2 mm layers or "supports off" when the file does not say). This is information only: nothing new is refused.
- Jobs: a job that is not printing now says what it is waiting for, in one line under its status on the table and on the phone card: waiting for approval, on hold, needs a filament slot chosen for each colour (with a button that opens the job's filament mapping), printer is offline, printer is busy (with the time the running print should end, when known), quiet hours (with the time they end), no printer can run it (naming the material or tag no printer has), or the reason the last dispatch was refused, shown until the next attempt. Offline and busy lines have a button that opens the printer. The line goes away when the cause is fixed. `GET /api/v1/jobs` and `GET /api/v1/jobs/{id}` carry it as `waiting_reason` (`code`, and where they apply `detail`, `until`, `printer_id`); it is worked out when the list is read and nothing is stored. A printer you are not allowed to see is never named or linked.
- New: when a Bambu printer's own camera reports a problem (spaghetti, first-layer defects, nozzle clumping, air printing, a shifted or collapsed print, a full waste chute), ODIN now raises an alert and lists it under Detections. ODIN reads the printer's own report over your local network and sends no picture anywhere. ODIN does not pause the print itself: the printer follows its own setting. Detections shows a Printer / Vigil source marker and filter; `GET /api/vision/detections` accepts `source`, and `GET /api/vision/stats` adds `by_source` with confirmed and dismissed counts.
- Adding a printer: a failed connection test now says why and what to do. ODIN tells apart a printer it could not reach, credentials the printer rejected, something at that address that is not the chosen printer type, and an address ODIN does not connect to; when it cannot tell, it says so and shows the checklist as before. The message never repeats the address, serial number, access code or API key. On the Printers page, saving a printer whose connection was not tested with the details entered, or whose last test failed, asks "Save anyway?" first. API: a failed `POST /api/printers/test-connection` carries `reason` (`unreachable`, `auth`, `not_this_type`, `blocked_address`, `control_disabled`, `unknown`) next to `success` and `error`; an address ODIN refuses is now answered as a failed test with `reason: "blocked_address"` instead of HTTP 400. Bambu LAN Only and Developer Mode cannot be seen by the test, so `control_disabled` is not sent yet; Anycubic tests always report `unknown`.

### Changed

- Pricing Calculator: the percentage it adds to cost is now correctly called Markup (it was labelled Margin), and the resulting margin is shown under the price. A Target margin field sets the same value the other way round. New optional selling-fee (percentage and fixed) and per-plate handling inputs; with these left at 0 every price is unchanged. Saved settings and prices are unchanged. The cost API also returns `markup_percent`, `selling_fees` and `margin_of_price_percent`.

### Fixed

- Shared print-file checks are faster in large libraries, and supported API previews now work on both `/api/...` and `/api/v1/...` without changing saved data.
- Long filament names wrap on small screens, catalogue controls and failure-correction forms are easier to use by touch, and Print Log notes expand to show the full text. Classic printer detail and dashboard now show catalogue names, import counts use the correct singular or plural, and failure corrections use the shared date format.

- The model library card now shows cost per item, matching the calculator. Before, a plate with several items showed the whole plate's cost. Price is also per item, cards say how many items fit on a plate, and a model markup of 0 is honoured.
- Print next ignores jobs without a model and unrelated work. Deleted production sources block only the affected products, so other products keep their stock plans and queue buttons.
- Fixed Print next: hide work in progress unless you can see every restricted part in the farm, and stop stock planning when saved production records are incomplete or belong to another farm.
- Operators and administrators can confirm prints after a restart. Changed records are checked again before recording resumes, answers saved before recording resumes survive another restart, and waiting screens and unverified print totals now explain their status.
- PostgreSQL installations can now save either answer to a print confirmation after a restart. If the records are busy, the question stays open so you can try again.
- Operators and administrators can now confirm a print after a restart on printers without an organization. Questions close when their records are closed while the printer is idle, and viewers can see both answer buttons disabled.
- After a restart during a print, ODIN no longer creates a second record for it. If it cannot be sure the print is the same one, it asks once in Dispatch Recovery and keeps one record while waiting. Live readings and fault alerts continue; changed records close the question with an explanation.
- A job's due date now shows as the day you picked in every time zone. Before, a job due Nov 20 could read as Nov 19 in the Timeline detail for anyone west of UTC, and the Jobs list counted "due today" and "overdue" from midnight UTC instead of your own calendar day. A job is now marked overdue (red row) only once its due day has passed where you are, not during the due day itself, and hovering the due badge shows the date.
- Audit Log: each entry now reads as a plain sentence ("newowner sent job 1 to Test X1C"), with the raw action and details one click away under "Raw record"; actions without a sentence yet look as before. A password sign-in now writes one audit entry instead of two: `auth.login` for a completed sign-in and `auth.login_failed` for a failed one (a correct password that still needs a second step keeps its single `login_success` entry). Existing entries are untouched; a SIEM rule or saved search that matched the old `login_failed` or `login_success` twins should match `auth.login_failed` and `auth.login`. The Export CSV button is no longer shown on licenses without audit export, instead of a disabled button.
- Live updates come back by themselves: when the page could not get its live-updates token (for example after several quick reloads, or while the server restarted) it stopped updating until reloaded. It now tries again after 5 seconds, backing off to once a minute.
- New O.D.I.N. mark: the eye now appears beside the name in the sidebar, the phone header and on the sign-in page, and as the browser tab, home-screen and installed-app icon. Installs without custom branding had no tab icon at all before. A white-labelled install (its own name or logo) is unchanged and never shows the O.D.I.N. mark.
- Agent retries with expiring API tokens now avoid duplicate writes. If retry protection cannot verify the caller, the write is refused with a retryable error; agent tokens can also check the server version.

---

name: O.D.I.N. v2.2.1
body:
ITAR mode hardening: every connection goes to the address that was checked.

### Security

- ITAR mode: a webhook is now sent to the address that was checked. O.D.I.N. looks the webhook's host name up once, checks that answer and connects to it; before, it looked the name up twice, and a name that answered with a local address first and an outside address second was contacted at the outside address. The built-in Telegram, Pushover and WhatsApp senders are checked and connected the same way. With ITAR mode on, a webhook to an address on your local network (10.x, 172.16-31.x, 192.168.x, or IPv6 unique-local) now works and can be saved by IP address; before, ITAR mode refused every webhook. Loopback and link-local addresses stay refused, and so do O.D.I.N.'s own ports on its own addresses. With ITAR mode on a webhook also cannot use the port number of the PostgreSQL server in `DATABASE_URL` (5432 if none is given) or of the go2rtc API in `ODIN_GO2RTC_API_URL` (80 or 443 if none is given), on any host. Nothing changes with ITAR mode off.
- ITAR mode: mail and MQTT now connect to the address that was checked. For the mail server (alerts, reports, password reset and welcome mail) and the MQTT broker (event republishing, its connection test and smart-plug commands), O.D.I.N. looks the host name up once, refuses it unless every address is on the local network, and connects to that address; an MQTT reconnect goes to the same address. Before, the name was checked and then looked up again to connect, so a name that changed its answer could receive the mail password, notifications, reports or plug commands. TLS still uses the configured host name. Nothing changes with ITAR mode off.
- ITAR mode: an Elegoo printer can no longer send O.D.I.N. to another address. The printer's WebSocket connection and the status read before a print is sent now refuse an HTTP redirect; before, a printer on the local network could answer with a redirect to an outside address and O.D.I.N. connected there. Nothing changes with ITAR mode off.
- ITAR mode: the camera relay (go2rtc) no longer starts with a camera list written before this start. If O.D.I.N. cannot write the camera configuration when the container starts (for example the volume is full), it now replaces the old file with one that has no cameras, and cameras stay off until the configuration can be written; if the old file cannot be replaced either, the container refuses to start and says why. Before, go2rtc started with the old file, which could still name a camera outside the local network from before ITAR mode was turned on. Two more cases are closed. If `GO2RTC_CONFIG` names a different file from the one go2rtc is started with, the container refuses to start under ITAR mode (unset it). A camera relay run as its own container (the enterprise layout) is outside what ITAR mode can verify: O.D.I.N. writes only local camera sources into the file that relay reads and asks it to restart at each start of the API container (a `WARNING` in the log if that fails), but you must restart that container yourself after turning ITAR mode on and should restrict its network to the camera subnet. See "What ITAR mode covers" in [ITAR mode](docs/ITAR_MODE.md). Nothing changes with ITAR mode off.
- `ODIN_ITAR_MODE` is now read the same way everywhere. On is `1`, `true`, `yes` or `on`; off is unset, empty, `0`, `false`, `no` or `off` (any letter case, spaces around the value are ignored). Any other value, for example `"1"` with the quotes included or `2`, now stops the container at start with a message that names the accepted values. Before, such a value could remove the proxy settings and print an ITAR message at container start while the server itself ran with ITAR mode off. If your setting is one of the accepted values nothing changes.
- ITAR mode now covers the PostgreSQL database connection. With `ODIN_ITAR_MODE=1`, O.D.I.N. refuses to start when `DATABASE_URL` (or `DATABASE_MAINTENANCE_URL`) names a PostgreSQL server that is not on the local network, and the backup and restore tools (`pg_dump`, `pg_restore`) are not started against one. It connects to the address it checked: for every database connection it opens, and for the backup tools, the server's name is looked up once, checked, and that address is given to the PostgreSQL driver (`hostaddr` / `PGHOSTADDR`), which then looks nothing up itself; the host name is still used to verify a TLS certificate. To make that certain, ITAR mode accepts one way of naming the server: one host in the address part of the URL (`postgresql://odin@postgres:5432/odin`), or no host for the local socket. **Now refused at start with ITAR mode on:** more than one host in the URL, `host=`, `hostaddr=`, `port=` or `service=` after the `?`, and `PGHOST`, `PGHOSTADDR`, `PGPORT`, `PGSERVICE` or `PGSERVICEFILE` in the container environment. The bundled `postgres` service is unaffected. SQLite installations and ITAR mode off are unchanged.
- ITAR mode: when O.D.I.N. refuses to start because a saved printer has an address outside the local network, you can now fix it without turning ITAR mode off. A new offline command, `python3 -m scripts.itar_printer_addresses` (`list`, `set PRINTER_ID ADDRESS`, `clear PRINTER_ID`), changes or removes the address in the database with nothing running, and writes an audit entry. It refuses to write while the O.D.I.N. API is answering on the same machine (unless `--force-running` is given), and it never overwrites an address that changed after it read it. The start-up message now points to it. See [ITAR mode](docs/ITAR_MODE.md).
- docs/ITAR_MODE.md now states the accepted values of `ODIN_ITAR_MODE`, the one multicast exception (printer discovery sends a link-local mDNS query to `224.0.0.251:5353`, which routers do not forward), how the PostgreSQL connection is checked and pinned, and the recovery steps above.

### Changed

- The container health check never uses a proxy, with ITAR mode on or off: the health check in the image and in the Compose files calls O.D.I.N. on `localhost` directly and ignores `HTTP_PROXY` and similar settings. This is intentional. Before, with a proxy setting in the container, the health check request could be sent to the proxy instead of to O.D.I.N.

### Fixed

- PostgreSQL installations: O.D.I.N. can read a printer's stored live state again. Before, features that check whether a printer is really printing before acting, such as Vigil's automatic pause, saw no state on PostgreSQL and did nothing. SQLite installations were not affected.

---

name: O.D.I.N. v2.2.0
body:
ODIN works on a phone, sets itself up faster, and checks filament before it prints. New: Jobs search, model library plates, maintenance and temperature alerts, material routing, Home Assistant print floor, timelapse status, more printers (OctoPrint, Elegoo, Ultimaker and Kobra S1 as Experimental), a license refresh button, and ITAR mode now covers the Square connection.

### Added

- Phone browsers, Classic theme: every button in a page, pop-up or stand-alone page is at least 44 px to the finger (switches look the same and take 44 px of space; small buttons inside a text field keep their size); a printer card's action buttons move to their own row instead of squeezing the printer's name. Desktop and tablet layouts are unchanged.
- Alerts: a long title on a single alert is shown on two lines and expands when pressed (grouped alerts already did this).
- Foundry cameras on a phone: the chosen camera's button is kept in view in the chooser strip.
- `GET /api/v1/jobs` takes several `status` values (`status=pending&status=scheduled`), `finished_since` (jobs that ended at or after a time) and `order=recent` (newest end first). They let the iPhone/iPad Queue load active jobs and today's finished jobs without being cut off by the default limit of 100 on servers with many jobs (needs the matching app update). The default order is unchanged. Cancelling or rejecting a job now records when that happened, so a job cancelled before it started counts as finished at that time, not at its creation.
- Inventory: an admin or operator can now correct a spool's empty-spool (core) weight after it was received, for example when a refill core is lighter than the 250 g default (`PATCH /api/spools/{id}` accepts `spool_weight_g`, 0 to 10000 g, and the Edit Spool dialog has the field). The change is audited with the old and new value. Remaining weight is kept as filament weight and is not changed; only later scale weighings use the new core weight.
- Spools whose remaining weight is not measured (unknown) now say "Not measured on this printer model" (loaded on a printer) or "Not measured yet" (in storage) instead of a blank or 0, with no bar and no low-stock colour. Editing such a spool no longer overwrites the unknown balance with 0 unless you type a weight. Printer slot tiles say the same for a slot that has a spool but no measured weight.
- The Jobs queue shows the pre-dispatch filament check for a scheduled job: "Filament check" on its row opens the read-only per-slot result (enough, short or not checked, with the grams left and needed) for the job's printer.
- Ultimaker S-series and Ultimaker 3 printers (Experimental, monitoring only). Add an Ultimaker printer (type Ultimaker, address only, no password or key) to monitor its state, bed and nozzle temperatures, job progress and camera; "Test connection" shows the printer's own variant and firmware. ODIN only reads from the printer (HTTP GET); sending jobs, pause, resume and stop are not available for this printer type yet, and the scheduler never assigns work to it. The camera URL defaults to `http://<printer>:8080/?action=stream` when the printer has its camera enabled and no camera URL set. The support is built from Ultimaker's public local API documentation and has not been verified on real hardware. Restart the container after adding an Ultimaker printer, changing its address, or deactivating it, so the new monitor process reads the new list (with the license fleet lock on, new printers start by themselves). See [Ultimaker](docs/printers/ultimaker.md).
- Elegoo job sending (Experimental). For Elegoo printers that speak SDCP (Centauri Carbon and similar), a platform administrator can now turn on job sending for a printer (`PUT /api/printers/{id}/experimental-actions`, audited). ODIN uploads a `.gcode` file to the printer and then sends the start command, and counts a start only when the printer answers that it accepted it; a timeout after the upload or the start is reported as unknown and is never re-sent. Monitoring, pause, resume, speed and stop work as before and need no opt-in. This support is built from Elegoo's public SDCP documentation and has not been verified on real hardware. See [Elegoo](docs/printers/elegoo.md).
- Pre-dispatch filament check: before a print starts, O.D.I.N. compares the grams each filament needs for that print (from the file's slice data, or the model's colour requirements, plus a margin, 10% by default) with what is left on the spool in the mapped slot. In `warn` mode (the default) dispatch goes ahead with a plain-words warning and an alert; in `hold` mode a short slot refuses the dispatch as `filament_short`, with the numbers; `off` skips the check. A slot with no estimate, no spool or no recorded weight is reported as unchecked and never holds. A superadmin sets the mode and margin (`PUT /api/config/filament-check`, audited); the dispatch dialog shows the per-slot result from `GET /api/jobs/{id}/filament-check`. On a printer you reach only because it is shared, the result says whether each slot has enough but not the owner's spool id or remaining weight. The same holds for the refusal, warning and alert when a job from another organization is sent to a shared printer.
- The Home Assistant status endpoint (`GET /api/integrations/home-assistant/status`, `schema_version` 2) now includes the print floor: each printer has `next_job` (name, held, estimated minutes, copies on the plate, filaments with the AMS slot each needs, plate, and an `ams_check` that compares the job with the loaded trays using the same check as dispatch) and `bench` (`clear_plate`, `blocked`, `held` or `paused`, with a plain reason; paused printers say whether it was a planned pause, a spaghetti pause or an error). The `fleet` object adds `today` (plates done and failed since local midnight), `queued_hours`, `queued_unestimated` and `next_unassigned` (up to five unassigned jobs). Existing keys are unchanged, nothing is written and no printer is contacted, and the same job visibility rules apply: a job the caller cannot list is not counted or shown, and controlled work is named "Controlled work" with its filaments, plate and AMS check withheld.
- Camera stills for dashboards: `GET /api/overlay/{printer_id}/snapshot?token=` returns one JPEG for a camera-only token, with the same checks as the overlay camera stream on every request. It opens no stream, so a dashboard that polls many cameras (Home Assistant) no longer runs into the stream limit and shows grey tiles. One camera token may now hold up to 16 live streams across printers (was 3); the per-printer and per-user limits are unchanged. The Home Assistant integration 0.1.2 uses the new route and falls back to the stream on older O.D.I.N. versions.
- Maintenance: ODIN now checks every hour and tells the people who can see a printer when a maintenance task is due soon or overdue, once per stage and not every hour; logging the service resets it, and alert preferences and quiet hours apply. A service can be logged for an earlier date (from 2020-01-01, not in the future). A printer with no maintenance task gets a default "General service" every 2000 print hours until you add one. The Maintenance page also shows each printer's failed-print rate for the last 30 and 90 days; cancelled prints are not counted.
- Per-printer timelapse capture status: `GET /api/printers/{id}/timelapse-status` reports whether a timelapse is recording, its frame count, the time of the last frame and, when it is not recording, the reason in plain words. The camera page shows it as a status line. Prints started outside O.D.I.N. (no matching O.D.I.N. job) are still not recorded, and the status says so.
- Temperature-anomaly alerts: while a print runs, O.D.I.N. now warns you when a nozzle or bed stays well below its target (default 15 C for 5 minutes, after an 8 minute warm-up), overshoots it, heats with no target set, or reads an impossible value. The warning is a printer error alert, so it follows your existing alert preferences and quiet hours. It is on by default and only alerts: it never pauses or stops a print. Platform admins can switch it off, or switch off single printers and change the thresholds, under Settings > Notifications > Temperature anomaly alerts (or `PUT /api/config/temperature-alerts` with `{"enabled": false}`).
- Klipper/Moonraker printers on the local network can now be found from the add-printer dialog: choose Klipper / Moonraker and press "Find Klipper printers on the network" (`POST /api/printers/discover/moonraker`, administrators with the `write:printers` scope). O.D.I.N. sends one mDNS query for `_moonraker._tcp`, offers only local-network addresses that pass the printer destination policy (also in ITAR mode), marks printers you have already added and, for printers that announced themselves, confirms them with one credential-free status request. Without multicast access (a container on the default Docker network) it returns an empty list and explains that discovery needs host networking or mDNS reflection. See [Moonraker discovery](docs/printers/moonraker-discovery.md).
- docs/NIST_800_171.md maps O.D.I.N. features to the NIST SP 800-171 Rev. 2 requirements they help you meet, with tier, ITAR-mode notes, your responsibilities and what is not provided. It is not a certification or attestation.
- Deleting a printer locks the shared Experimental opt-in store before reading it, so a concurrent revocation for another printer cannot be overwritten on PostgreSQL.
- OctoPrint monitoring retries start observation after an unreadable job or missing filename, and establishes an active attempt when first observed paused so resume and progress remain tracked.
- Printer detail pages show the Experimental badge, warning and administrator opt-in, with immediate refresh after changing the setting.
- OctoPrint printers (Experimental). Add an OctoPrint server as a printer (type OctoPrint, with an application key created in OctoPrint) to monitor its state, temperatures, progress and camera. Sending jobs and resume stay off until a platform administrator turns them on for that printer; pause and stop always work. The support is built from OctoPrint's public REST API documentation and has not been verified on real hardware. Restart the container after adding an OctoPrint printer, changing its address or key, or deactivating it, so the monitor process reads the new list (the same as PrusaLink; with the license fleet lock on, new printers start by themselves). See [OctoPrint](docs/printers/octoprint.md).
- Printer support levels. Every printer type is now Supported, Experimental or Not supported, and `GET /api/printers` and the printer detail report `support_level` and `experimental_actions_enabled`. On an Experimental printer, ODIN refuses job sending and printer controls (resume, speed, fan, lights, clear errors, skip objects) until a platform administrator turns them on for that printer (`PUT /api/printers/{id}/experimental-actions`, audited). Pause and stop always work, so a running print can always be held or stopped, and monitoring always works. The printer card shows an Experimental badge and the add-printer list labels Experimental types. OctoPrint is the first Experimental type, and every other type keeps what it does today.
- Printer-card plate pictures now retry up to six times at ten-second intervals when unavailable, so a background cache build can populate the picture without changing prints or toggling the preference. Retries stop after success, when pictures are disabled, or when the card unmounts; changing prints starts a fresh attempt.
- Model library search and plate viewer. The Models page has a Filters panel (model, file or project name; material; sliced-for printer model; plate count range; "printed OK on printer"), and the model list endpoints (`GET /api/models`, `GET /api/models-with-pricing`) and `GET /api/print-files` accept `q`, `material`, `printer_model`, `plates_min`, `plates_max` and `printed_on_printer`. Filtering happens on the server under the list's existing organization, controlled-part and Education rules, so a file you cannot see is never matched; Education-owned files are not searchable by file facts. Each model card has a Plates view that lists every plate with its picture, filaments with colour and grams, print time, weight, layer height, slicer warnings and the slicer name and version.
- Sliced 3MF files now keep each plate's picture and slice facts (filaments, print time, weight, layer height, slicer warnings, slicer name and version). They are read when a file is uploaded, or the first time they are requested for an older file, and cached on disk by file hash. `GET /api/print-files/{id}/plates` returns the facts, and `GET /api/print-files/{id}/plates/{plate}/thumbnail` returns a plate's picture. Both follow the same access rules as the 3D preview. A new per-user option on the Printers page, "Show plate picture on printer cards" (off by default), shows a small picture of the running plate on printing and paused printer cards. It comes from `GET /api/printers/{id}/current-plate-thumbnail`, which is separate from printer status, live events, the overlay and Home Assistant.
- Confirming a cleared plate now always counts: `POST /api/printers/{id}/plate-cleared` records the confirmation against the printer's last finished print even when no job was waiting for it, so `plate_clear_confirmed_at` is set (Home Assistant and the printer card can show the printer as ready). The confirmation is dropped again as soon as the next print starts. Nothing is recorded while the printer is printing or paused, or when it has no finished print.
- Kobra S1 starts now check the printer's start service with a confirmed missing file before sending the real print. An unanswered check leaves the job queued and releases the printer; results are recorded in the job timeline and audit log. Sending remains off unless the server operator enables it.
- ITAR mode can now allow a named identity provider for single sign-on: set `ODIN_ITAR_ALLOWED_IDP_HOSTS` to the exact host names (for example `login.microsoftonline.us,graph.microsoft.us` for Microsoft Entra ID in GCC High, at most 8, no wildcards or IP addresses). Only O.D.I.N.'s sign-in client may reach those hosts; webhooks, the license server, Spoolman, email and every other outbound connection still refuse public addresses. Every allowed sign-in request is recorded in the audit log, an identity provider whose endpoints point at an unlisted host is refused, and O.D.I.N. refuses to start in ITAR mode if SSO is enabled with an identity provider that is neither on the local network nor allowed. See [ITAR mode](docs/ITAR_MODE.md).
- Settings > License has a **Refresh license** button (administrators). One click asks the O.D.I.N. license portal once for your latest license file and says in plain words what it found: renewed, not renewed yet, canceled, or no longer active. From 7 days before a license file ends, a "Renewal due" banner reminds administrators to click it. After a refresh the banner keeps showing the portal's answer until the next refresh, including "Pro features stop on {date}" for a canceled subscription and "Pro has ended" with a link to support@runsodin.com. O.D.I.N. still never contacts the license portal on its own. Superadmins can read that answer from `GET /api/license/last-refresh` (`status`, `at`, `expires_at`); the public `GET /api/license` does not include it, because it shows billing state. If the portal's answer and the license file it sends disagree (for example "renewed" with a license that has already ended), nothing is installed.
- O.D.I.N. now installs a signed replacement license that ends earlier than the installed one (for example after a cancellation), or, through Refresh license only, one that has already ended (a refund or chargeback: the server drops to Community and stays there after a restart, and the next refresh installs a valid file again if entitlement returns), as long as the portal issued it after the installed file. A signed license for the same key that was issued before the installed one is refused with a clear message, including when it is uploaded as a file.

### Changed

- Vigil's training-data collection is now sampled and bounded. It saves one frame every 120 seconds per printer instead of one on every detection tick (global `training_capture_interval_sec`, per-printer `training_interval_sec`), plus up to three frames around each confirmed detection. An optional per-printer bed crop (Settings, Vigil AI) is applied to training frames only; detection frames stay full size. Collection pauses, with one alert to platform administrators, while the frames volume has less than `training_min_free_gb` (default 2 GB) free, and resumes by itself. Prints of a model whose category is `no-training` are never collected.
- Jobs page: it opens on the queue (submitted, rejected, pending, scheduled, printing and paused jobs) instead of the first 100 jobs in queue order, which on a farm with many jobs could hide every pending job. History (completed, failed, cancelled) is its own choice, newest first, 50 at a time with Load more, and the page says "Showing 50 of 212" instead of cutting the list off silently. Search now runs on the server and finds a job by number (`218`, `#218`, `job 218`), name, printer name or nickname, or order number, among the jobs you are allowed to see. You can filter by printer (or Unassigned) and show held jobs only; filters and search are kept in the page address, and `/jobs?job=218` opens that job even when it is outside the filter. Every row shows `Job <number>`, queue position reads `Queue 3`, held jobs carry a Held badge, and pending and submitted jobs can be cancelled from their row. `GET /api/v1/jobs` also takes `q`, `held` and `unassigned` and always sends the number of matching jobs in an `X-Total-Count` header; the response body is unchanged. `POST /api/v1/jobs/{id}/cancel` now also cancels a job awaiting approval, as bulk cancel already did.

### Fixed

- Home Assistant day totals compare parsed completion times against local midnight, so Moonraker ISO timestamps and timestamps with offsets count on the correct day alongside naive UTC timestamps.
- Vigil training capture now verifies a print's job link when controlled data exists and rechecks controlled status before every sampled or burst frame write. Pending review advances correctly under React StrictMode. The training guide now correctly states that labelled frames also expire under the retention setting.
- License refresh refuses no-entitlement replacements with unverified evidence or a different key, including files ending within the clock allowance. Different files for the same key must have a newer issue time; a different file with the same issue time (a plan or limit change on a license without a subscription) is installed only when it does not end later than the installed one, so it can never bring back a refunded or canceled plan. Refused replacements leave the installed license unchanged.
- When the license folder's `odin.license` is only a link to the file set in `ODIN_LICENSE_FILE`, refreshing, activating or uploading a license is now refused with a message that the license file is managed outside O.D.I.N. and must be replaced there. Before, the link was replaced, the server kept reading the old file, and the refresh reported success.
- Settings > Notifications: the Alert Preferences table lays out as a table again (alert type, then In-App, Push and Email side by side). A malformed layout rule had stacked the three switches under each alert at tablet and desktop widths (768 px and up; on a phone they stack by design). The same fault is fixed in the Education cost-center manager's two-column layout and member rows.
- The scheduler now routes by filament material, not only colour. By default (`require`), a job is only assigned to a printer whose loaded filament includes every material the job needs (taken from the sliced file, otherwise from the job's filament type). A printer or job with no recorded material is never excluded, so installs that don't record materials see no change. **Behaviour change on upgrade for farms that do record materials (every Bambu AMS farm):** a job whose material is not loaded on any printer now waits in the queue with a reason, where it used to be assigned and then refused at dispatch (or, on other printer types, printed in the wrong material). Switch Filament routing to `prefer` or `off` to keep the old assignment behaviour. A job that no printer can take stays queued, and the scheduler run notes and the "Job could not be scheduled" alert say which material is missing; a job pinned to a printer that lacks the material also stays queued and is never moved. To switch it off, set **Settings > General > Scheduler Settings > Filament routing** to **Off** (colour scoring only, as before), or to **Prefer** (matching material ranks first but nothing is excluded). Only a platform administrator can change it, and each change is audited.

### Security

- Vigil no longer saves training-data frames while a controlled job is printing. Viewing those frames was already limited to platform administrators inside the job's audience, but the pictures were still written to disk for the retention period. If the check cannot be made, no frame is saved.
- Mapping a product to a Square variation that Square tracks by availability now says what to change ("Track by stock count" for that location) instead of a generic inventory-tracking message; the mapping panel says the same.
- ITAR mode now also covers Square: with `ODIN_ITAR_MODE=1` every Square call is refused before any network use, and ODIN refuses to start while a Square connection is stored. Previously an administrator could connect Square on such a server.
- ITAR mode now refuses to start when single sign-on uses the built-in Microsoft or Google preset without being on the allowed identity-provider list. The sign-in itself was already blocked; the problem now shows at start-up instead of at the first sign-in.

name: O.D.I.N. v2.1.1
body:
Hotfix: the iPhone/iPad Queue could fail to load after a Kobra/Moonraker print finished. Job dates are now stored and sent in one form.

### Fixed

- The iPhone/iPad app's Queue could fail to load ("The data couldn't be read because it isn't in the correct format") after a Kobra/Moonraker print finished, because that print's start and end times were stored with a timezone. O.D.I.N. now stores Moonraker times in the same form as every other printer, and the job list and job detail endpoints send every job date in one form (`YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS`, UTC), including for rows already stored the old way. Stored rows are not rewritten. A print that started before the upgrade and finishes after it still gets its duration in the print history.

name: O.D.I.N. v2.1.0
body:
First release-train release: Shane's farm runs each train release about a day before customers. Fixes auto-dispatch on Bambu and PrusaLink printers, keeps a P1S slot colour after a tray change, lets a job's AMS mapping be written back as it is read, and lets an opened RFID roll merge into a sealed record received later. The Terms now allow service providers to run O.D.I.N. for licensed customers.

### Fixed

- Auto-dispatch (`AUTO_DISPATCH=true`) never dispatched to Bambu or PrusaLink printers: their monitors imported a module that doesn't exist, and the error was only logged. They now use the real dispatcher, and every dispatch still passes the same admission checks. Auto-dispatch stays off by default.
- P1S: after a filament slot was set from O.D.I.N., the printer page showed the slot as black (`000000`) until the next AMS report, and an AMS report with no colour (`00000000`) could then wipe it. The chosen colour is now stored when the slot is set, and a report with no colour no longer replaces it. A real colour change on the printer still wins. A tray reported with no colour is now shown as no colour instead of black.
- `PATCH /api/jobs/{id}` now accepts `ams_mapping` in the same vector form that `GET` returns (for example `[3]`), so a mapping read from the API can be written back. The vector must match the file's filament layout exactly; the existing slot-entry form still works, and both get the same validation.
- Inventory: an opened RFID roll can now be merged into a sealed record that was received after the roll was first seen, when that record is still unassigned sealed stock of the same product line, material and colour and has no usage history. Before, only records listed when the roll was first read could be targets, so the same purchase could be counted twice. Rolls that already have job usage, drying history or a Spoolman link are still refused, with a reason.

### Changed

- Terms of Service: managed service providers, integrators and contractors may install and operate O.D.I.N. for a customer who holds the license, on that customer's own infrastructure or in an environment dedicated to that customer (new Section 3.7). Offering O.D.I.N. as a hosted, multi-tenant or software-as-a-service product, or running one Instance for several customers, is still not allowed (Sections 3.5 and 14.2). The Terms no longer say the BSL 1.1 requires that restriction; it is a term of this Agreement.
- Terms of Service, payments (Section 5): online orders are sold by Paddle as merchant of record, which handles taxes, payment and refunds under its buyer terms. Pro is a monthly or annual subscription that renews automatically until cancelled, and cancelling takes effect at the end of the paid period. The 30-day written cancellation notice and the 30-day annual refund are replaced by a 14-day free trial, with payments non-refundable except where law or Paddle's buyer terms give a right to a refund. Licenses already bought by invoice keep their invoiced term. Contact addresses in the Terms are now support@runsodin.com.
- Terms of Service: "Site" is now defined (one location or one environment of one legal entity; each customer of a service provider is its own Site). An Enterprise license key covers up to three Instances per licensed Site: production plus staging, test or disaster recovery. Keys bought through an authorized reseller are licensed by JLLS Holdings LLC directly to the end customer.
- Terms of Service and FEATURES.md list the current Enterprise features (tamper-evident audit log with SIEM streaming, part traceability with certificates of conformance, controlled-part handling), and the Terms state that no feature is a CMMC, FedRAMP or other certification. They also correct an earlier statement: organization management is included in Education and Enterprise, not in every tier (MFA, IP allowlisting and GDPR export/anonymization remain in every tier).
- README points support to support@runsodin.com, and README and CONTRIBUTING no longer link the Discord invite, which no longer works.
- SECURITY.md lists 2.x as the supported release line (it still said 1.0.x).

- License checks: if the server's clock jumps more than 24 hours forward while O.D.I.N. is running, the license is treated as unverified, and paid features pause, until the clock has read steadily for a few seconds; the clock check then recovers on its own (a license whose expiry date has passed by the new time stays expired). A clock that is already wrong when O.D.I.N. starts is judged as before. The license status reports the clock error while it lasts. Local password login is never affected.
- License checks: a license file that exists but can't be read (for example a permissions problem on `/data/odin.license`) now shows as "verification unavailable" with the read error, instead of silently falling back to Community as if no license were installed.

### Internal

- Groundwork for per-printer license limits is included but switched off (`ODIN_LICENSE_FLEET_LOCK_ENABLED` is unset): with it off, printer monitoring and dispatch behave exactly as in 2.0.52.
- Release process: each train release now runs on Shane's own farm for about 24 hours before it is offered to customers (hotfixes soak for about an hour).

name: O.D.I.N. v2.0.52
body:
Dispatch refusals now say why printer readiness could not be confirmed, and printer connection tests and AMS sync no longer leave Bambu connections open after an error.

### Fixed

- When a dispatch is refused because O.D.I.N. could not confirm the printer was ready, the message now names the reason, for example `not_ready_or_unreachable`, `no_reply_before_deadline`, `reply_after_deadline`, or `read_error:` followed by the error type. Before, it said only "Fresh printer readiness was not confirmed". The decision is unchanged: nothing is sent unless readiness is confirmed. Reasons come from a fixed list, and anything unrecognized is shown as `printer_not_ready`.
- Testing a Bambu printer's connection (from the printer page or setup) and syncing filament slots (Bambu and Moonraker) now always close the printer connection, including when an error occurs. Before, an error could leave the connection open, and on a Bambu printer that holds one of its few connection slots.
- Bambu: if O.D.I.N. connects to a printer but then fails while recovering that printer's interrupted jobs, it now closes that connection instead of leaving it running unused.
- Bambu: when a final check refuses the start just before the print command (for example a filament slot or printer state that no longer matches, or a check that could not complete), the dispatch is now closed without sending anything and the printer can be retried, the same as with the older connection method. Before, this left the dispatch marked uncertain and the printer needed manual recovery, although no print command had been sent. Recovery is still required if a maintenance hold caused the refusal, if the check itself stopped with an unexpected error, or if the result of a print command is unknown.

### Release tooling

- The validation setup now refuses to install into an environment folder that is a symbolic link, and names the link's target. Before, a linked folder could make validation install into, and fail on, another workspace.

name: O.D.I.N. v2.0.51
body:
Adds a read-only status endpoint for Home Assistant, runs Bambu uploads one at a time, lets a printer be retried after an upload that failed before any print command (when safety checks and the claim release succeed), and refuses backups whose recovery history could be edited.

### Added

- A read-only fleet status endpoint for Home Assistant: `GET /api/v1/integrations/home-assistant/status`. It returns each printer's status, progress, layer, time remaining, job name, last error and whether it is online, plus fleet counts and queue length. It reads only O.D.I.N.'s database and never contacts a printer, so polling it does not use printer connections. For Home Assistant, use an API token with `read:printers` and `read:jobs` (or broad `read`). Job names and error text for controlled work are hidden from callers who cannot see it.
- A Home Assistant custom integration (`integrations/home-assistant/`, installed manually for now) that reads this endpoint: one device per printer with status, progress, finish time, job, layers, online and problem sensors, an error event, fleet counts, and optional cameras through O.D.I.N.'s camera relay with a camera-only token. It has no controls.

### Fixed

- Bambu printers: an O.D.I.N. installation now runs one file upload at a time, so uploads to different printers no longer overlap on the same network. A second upload waits up to 15 minutes by default (`ODIN_FTPS_UPLOAD_WAIT_SECONDS`), and its dispatch shows "Waiting for another printer's upload to finish..." after two seconds. If the waiting limit is reached (two uploads per O.D.I.N. process by default, `ODIN_FTPS_UPLOAD_MAX_WAITERS`), or the upload slot can't be opened, the dispatch stops at once without sending anything, and it can be retried once the claim is released. `ODIN_FTPS_UPLOAD_SERIAL=0` turns this off.
- A Bambu upload that fails no longer blocks the printer. Before, a failed or timed-out upload marked the dispatch as uncertain, and the printer needed manual recovery even though no print command had been sent. Now, when the upload fails before any print command, the dispatch is closed and the printer can be retried, provided the safety checks pass and the claim release is saved. Recovery is still required if a maintenance hold was set during the upload, the hold can't be read, an Education reservation can't be cancelled, the claim release can't be saved, the printer's target ownership changed, or the outcome is otherwise unknown. A failure after the print command was attempted still requires recovery, as before.
- Backup validation now refuses a backup whose dispatch recovery history (migrations 038 and 056) is missing its protection against edits and deletes. Before, such a backup was accepted and would restore a history that could be changed.

### Release tooling

- The Education backup gate now runs every SQLite backup and restore test, not one file, and two of those tests were brought up to date with migration 056.

Enterprise gets a tamper-evident audit log with SIEM streaming and part traceability with signed certificates; Education gets classes, training sign-off, program reports, roster sync and term retention; SSO and license connections always go to the checked address.

### Security

- OIDC, Classroom and license-server requests connect to the DNS address validated by ITAR policy. Requests use a bounded worker pool and a total timeout covering queue wait, DNS and response streaming, with response size limits.
- ITAR refuses Teredo (`2001::/32`), 6to4 (`2002::/16`) and NAT64 (`64:ff9b::/96`, `64:ff9b:1::/48`) addresses, plus special-use ranges Python classifies as private, including `0.0.0.0`, `198.18.0.0/15` and `192.0.0.0/24`. Internal services using these ranges must move to RFC1918 IPv4 or ULA IPv6 addresses.
- OIDC sign-in allows 30 attempts per minute per client IP, shared across API aliases. Clients behind a proxy configured in `ODIN_TRUSTED_PROXIES` have separate limits; forwarding headers from other peers do not change the limit key.

### Added

- Enterprise audit verification, daily integrity alerts, signed JSON Lines exports, and Settings controls for syslog TCP/TLS or authenticated HTTPS SIEM streaming. Existing audit records receive a salted SHA-256 chain. GDPR erasure and age-based cleanup retain authenticated receipts and checkpoints. Backups can include audit keys, and released backups remain restorable. See [audit integrity operations](docs/AUDIT_INTEGRITY.md).
- Education and Enterprise training sign-off before student printing: printer-specific requirements, quizzes, instructor assessment, expiry, revocation, and a Training workspace. Checks run at submission, approval, scheduling and physical dispatch. Training requirements cover all classes sharing a printer; requirement changes warn about affected completions. See [Training before printing](docs/education/training-signoff.md).
- Education and Enterprise classes and assignments: term-labelled classes, due dates, print time/material limits, student submission quotas, optional instructor-authorized auto-approval, feedback and grades, and private portfolios with thumbnails and timelapses. Unassigned submissions retain their existing behavior.
- Education and Enterprise program funding reports by cost center, class and term: students served, verified print totals, material use, estimated cost, success rate and teaching hours. CSV/PDF exports and scheduled email use the same metrics, with school timezones, small-cell suppression and recipient checks. A draft Perkins V worksheet is disabled by default while field definitions remain unconfirmed. See [program reporting definitions](docs/EDUCATION_PROGRAM_REPORTS.md).
- Education and Enterprise Google Classroom and Canvas roster imports with classroom sign-in. - Enterprise part traceability: retained file hashes and manufacturing evidence, operator inspections, inspection policies, delivery receipts, signed PDF certificates, and date-range ZIP exports. The audit log records who watches cameras and timelapses; Bambu health codes come from Bambu's own lists; ODIN restarts safely during prints.

### Added

- The audit log records who watches a printer's live camera (WebRTC, MJPEG, snapshots and the OBS overlay) or plays a timelapse, with their IP address. A view is recorded when it starts and then at most once every 15 minutes per person, place and sign-in method, not frame by frame. If the record can't be written, the camera image isn't served.
- Automatic dispatches are labelled as the scheduler in the audit log, with the IDs of who queued and approved the job.
- SSO sign-ins, successful and failed, record the username, and the audit CSV fills its User ID and Username columns for successful SSO sign-ins. Erasing a user removes the username and IP address.
- Bambu health (HMS) and print error codes are decoded offline from Bambu's own per-model lists. Severity comes from the code: fatal and serious notices alert and can fail a job; common and info notices are shown but don't alert or fail jobs. Current faults are kept apart from history.

### Changed

- API and agent tokens, including the global API key, can't resume a printer with a current fatal or serious HMS fault or an open Vigil auto-pause. ODIN returns a named refusal, records who asked and why, and a person resumes from the web app. Signed-in sessions keep their controls.
- Resume responses no longer suggest pause to tokens that can't call it.

### Fixed

- Downloading a timelapse through its video link is now audited like the download button.
- After ODIN restarts, Vigil doesn't auto-pause a print until the printer has reported its live state since the restart and Vigil has analysed the print for at least 3 frames and 60 seconds. An unknown layer no longer turns on first-layer checks, and Vigil re-checks the printer's live state just before pausing.
- A replayed (retained) HMS report after a restart or reconnect can't mark a running print failed. A stopping code fails the job only when a fresh report shows the printer stopped.

Foundry, a new look you can switch on; plates up to 256 MiB of G-code; plan a filament load for held jobs before loading it.

### Added

- Foundry, a new look for the web app, built from the design board. Classic stays the default and looks exactly as before; choose Foundry from the theme button in the header. Foundry brings:
  - the Floor page: printer cards with compact slot tiles, a banner for printers that need you, live cameras with a printer switcher, and a "Next 12 hours" schedule lane;
  - Comfortable and Compact views on the Floor and Printers pages;
  - every other page restyled, with layouts that work on phones and tablets.
- Held jobs can carry a planned tray mapping for filament that isn't loaded yet, so you can queue several jobs for one filament load. Releasing the hold checks the trays. If they don't match, the job stays held and says what to load, for example "load PETG in AMS 1 slot 2". Dispatch still checks the live trays as before.
- Repeating a job whose tray plan no longer matches the loaded trays creates the repeat held, with what to load, instead of queueing it unchecked.

### Changed

- Large multicolour plates: up to 256 MiB of plate G-code (was 96 MiB), and print-file and Education uploads up to 160 MiB (was 100 MB). Files are read as a stream, so memory doesn't grow with the plate. A 256 MiB plate takes about 20 to 30 seconds to check on two cores, and the check finishes before the printer is contacted. Zip size, member and expansion limits still apply, plus a compression-ratio limit for large members.
- Each dispatch checks a file's filament sources once instead of twice.

### Fixed

- A scheduled job more than 2 hours late could be moved back to pending while its dispatch was still being prepared. The stale-schedule cleanup now leaves jobs with a dispatch in progress alone.
- Selection checkboxes, label links, scrollable tables and colour swatches have accessible names.
